claims.text: A uniform dispersion of fine oxide precipitates along grain boundaries enhances high-temperature plastic strain in tungsten-based fusion plasma-facing alloys.
A uniform dispersion of fine oxide precipitates along grain boundaries enhances high-temperature toughness in tungsten-based fusion plasma-facing alloys.
Fine oxide precipitates pin dislocations in tungsten alloys.
Fine oxide precipitates retard dynamic recrystallization in tungsten alloys.
The unmodified polycrystalline tungsten alloy has a relatively coarse grain-boundary structure.
A uniform sub-micron oxide dispersion can be introduced through controlled powder metallurgy or modified additive manufacturing.
Mechanical testing at approximately 1000–1300°C is representative of fusion plasma-facing conditions.
Fine, stable oxide precipitates enriched at grain boundaries act as effective obstacles to dislocation motion.
Dynamic recrystallization typically reduces tungsten-alloy toughness at high temperatures.
Dislocation pinning by oxide particles delays the onset of dynamic recrystallization.
The oxide dispersion maintains a higher density of effective slip systems.
Maintaining a higher density of effective slip systems allows the alloy to accommodate more plastic strain.
Relative to the baseline alloy, the oxide-dispersed alloy will show a statistically significant delay in dynamic-recrystallization onset.
Relative to the baseline alloy, the oxide-dispersed alloy will exhibit greater plastic strain before failure.
Relative to the baseline alloy, the oxide-dispersed alloy will maintain higher toughness under identical high-temperature loading.
The hypothesis is restricted to tungsten alloys with similar grain-size distributions and temperatures of approximately 1000–1300°C.
The hypothesized effect may fail above the oxide precipitates' stability range.
A non-uniform or coarsened oxide dispersion may eliminate the hypothesized effect.
Variations in precipitate distribution, grain size, and irradiation exposure may alter the magnitude of the improvement.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant recrystallization delay and improvements in plastic strain and toughness under identical conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
